decisions.reason: The indoor air quality module builds directly on the firm's established sensor, firmware and binding knowledge, so it stays easy to maintain and fits the ongoing demand for environmental measurement.
As the current generation of a long-running analog measurement line, it rests on deep accumulated knowledge and would only be retired by a successor, which is not yet due.
The MQTT proxy extends the core API-generation competence to a key IoT protocol at low cost, though native MQTT support in newer firmware could eventually make it redundant.
The CO2 module fits squarely within the firm's sensor-integration expertise, and demand for CO2 monitoring remains strong, even if a hardware-generation refresh could later replace it.

The touch panel accessory is further from core module knowledge and gives weaker learning feedback, but it still complements the display and prototyping kits, so it is kept while remaining under review.
